raw_response:
As of April 17, 2026, I would stay with the local main grain rotation: winter wheat followed by summer maize. I am in Quzhou County, where wheat and maize still dominate, and more than 80% of fields in the county have been in that annual rotation; recent local “吨半粮” work in Quzhou also showed this rotation can still give strong yields with tighter water and nitrogen use than the old heavy-input way. Because Quzhou is in a groundwater-stressed area and most rain comes in the maize season, I would not spread myself across too many crops this year. I would keep the plan simple, use a good improved wheat variety and a hybrid maize variety, hold nitrogen around the local efficient range, irrigate wheat twice and maize once, and aim for steady yield instead of chasing the very top demonstration-field numbers. Since no total land area was given, I am expressing my plan on a per-mu basis. Sources I used: [MOA on Quzhou “绿色吨半粮”](https://www.moa.gov.cn/xw/qg/202411/t20241104_6465572.htm), [China Agricultural University Quzhou station](https://qzsyz.cau.edu.cn/art/2024/10/8/art_46317_1039835.html), and a Quzhou/North China Plain study noting that most local fields are in winter-wheat/summer-maize rotation and most rainfall falls in the maize season: [Scientific Reports](https://www.nature.com/articles/srep41587).
